reviewed_by: agent self-review (code and security review by a human is still pending)
how_the_baseline_was_obtained: The availability-loss threshold is carried forward from the reviewed 1.3.0 clean run because 1.4.0 changes per-case outcome labels for benign controls and RT-011 only. Re-run artifacts for the current tree are saved next to the gate output.

availability_loss.basis: Three cases declare an availability objective. RT-016 (rank displacement) and RT-018 (oversized evidence) drop the authoritative record, so 2/3 degrade by construction; RT-012 preserves it because the per-platform cap drops only a decoy. The bound is the reviewed baseline count, so the gate fails only if availability loss grows beyond what has been reviewed.
availability_loss.uncertainty: Single deterministic run over small synthetic fixtures. This is a regression bound, not a security budget, not an availability guarantee and not a measurement of any real corpus. It carries no confidence interval and should be re-reviewed whenever a case or the ranking/budget code changes.

note: Only availability_loss is treated as a non-critical threshold. Every other entry above is a hard gate, because a critical consequence, a benign false positive or a wrong benign answer is not a quantity to be budgeted.
